name: Deep Strike
strategy: Deploy reserve formations into unexpected battlefield positions, launch flanking attacks, and establish forward landing zones.
designNote: Deep Strike changes where ordinary reinforcements may arrive. It does not create an additional Reserve pool or raise the universal reinforcement allowance.

deepStrikeReserve.rule: All Units designated as Reserve under the universal Staggered Deployment rules form one shared Reserve pool. An army with Deep Strike does not designate a second or separate Deep Strike Reserve. Any eligible Unit in that pool may enter normally or through an appropriate Deep Strike Command.
theseUnits: Count toward the universal mandatory Reserve Unit count, not a separate Reserve Point Value limit.
Are included in the army’s normal Points, Recruitment Slot, and composition limits.
Begin the battle off the battlefield.
Cannot perform actions or use abilities while in Reserve unless explicitly permitted.
May enter normally beginning in Round 1, or through a selected Deep Strike Command beginning in Round 2.
A Deep Strike arrival counts against that Round’s normal reinforcement allowance unless a rule expressly says otherwise.
additionalRules: Half of the army’s purchased Units, rounded up, must begin in Reserve under universal Staggered Deployment rules; if the army includes a Headquarters Unit, at least one must deploy normally.
Large Assets may arrive as ordinary Reserves, but may arrive using Deep Strike deployment only through Heavy Descent or another ability expressly permitting it.

procedure: During the Movement Phase, select an eligible Unit still in Reserve and declare an eligible Deep Strike deployment Command. Pay the Command’s CP cost and exhaust its card as normal.
Count this Unit against the current Round’s normal reinforcement allowance.

At the end of the Movement Phase, place that Unit at a legal location permitted by the Command, rather than the ordinary deployment zone. If other Reserve Units arrive, place them in the normal alternating placement order.
The Unit does not receive a Movement activation upon entry.
defaultPlacementRequirements: Wholly more than 9" from every enemy Model.
In legal positions with normal Unit coherency.
arrivingFromDeepStrikeReserve.note: Unless a Command says otherwise, the arriving Unit must satisfy the above placement requirements. Deep Strike deployment begins in Round 2.

unitArrivingThroughDeepStrike: Counts as having voluntarily Moved during that Movement Phase.
Cannot make additional Moves, Charge, Disengage, or Blink during the Round in which it arrives.
Cannot control or contest objectives until the following Round.
May make otherwise eligible ranged or Spell Attacks during the Assault Phase.
Cannot use a Heavy Attack that requires it not to have Moved, unless an ability explicitly permits otherwise.
additionalRules: Only one Unit may arrive through Deep Strike deployment Commands per Round. Other arriving Units may use ordinary Reserve deployment, up to the Round’s total allowance.
If a legal insertion position is unavailable, the Unit cannot be deployed using that Command; it remains in Reserve.
A player cannot declare an illegal placement, and no extra deployment allowance is granted.

commands.name: Forward Insertion
commands.effect: Designate one eligible Reserve Unit to deploy at the end of this Movement Phase using the normal Deep Strike placement rules. It may be placed anywhere on the battlefield that satisfies those rules. Counts toward the normal reinforcement allowance.

commands.name: Landing Fire
commands.effect: One friendly Unit that arrived through Deep Strike this Round gains Accurate 2 and Pinpoint on its next ranged Attack this Phase. This Command does not override Heavy restrictions.

commands.name: Flanking Insertion
commands.effect: Designate one eligible Reserve Unit to deploy at the end of this Movement Phase wholly within 3" of any battlefield edge and more than 6" from every enemy Model. It may enter the enemy deployment zone. All other arrival restrictions apply. Counts toward the normal reinforcement allowance.

commands.name: Heavy Descent
commands.effect: Designate one eligible Reserve Unit, including a Large Asset, to deploy at the end of this Movement Phase using normal Deep Strike placement rules. The Unit gains Tough 2 against the first Attack it suffers before the beginning of its next Movement activation. Counts toward the normal reinforcement allowance.

commands.name: Signal Beacon
commands.effect: Choose one friendly Unit already on the battlefield. During this Movement Phase, the next friendly Unit designated to arrive through Deep Strike within Short of that Unit may be placed more than 6" from enemy Models instead of 9". All other placement restrictions apply.

commandClarifications.clarification: Provides basic forward deployment, allowing a Unit to bypass the distance and terrain between the player’s deployment zone and a legal insertion point.
Improves a recently inserted Unit’s ranged attack. Any eligible Unit with a ranged weapon may benefit, not only Ranged Infantry.
Provides alternate access to battlefield edges, including enemy deployment territory, subject to its more-than-6" exclusion distance.
Is the usual Deep Strike method for Large Assets. Its Tough bonus is temporary and does not override Heavy weapon restrictions.

Must be used during the Movement Phase before declaring the insertion it modifies. The designated insertion still requires a separate Deep Strike deployment Command and still consumes one of that Round’s reinforcement allowances. Signal Beacon does not insert an additional Unit by itself.

doctrineIdentity: Deep Strike rewards flexible reserve arrival, battlefield penetration, and unexpected angles of attack. Unlike Alpha Strike, it does not accelerate the overall reinforcement schedule; its advantage is positional, and it can use that advantage repeatedly from Round 2 onward while sufficient Reserve Units and Commands remain.

distinctionFromOtherDoctrines.distinction: Improves the movement of Units already on the battlefield.
Uses friendly Units to create additional movement opportunities.
Maximizes early-Round offense and can bring in one extra Round 1 reinforcement.
Changes where purchased Reserve Units enter the battle, within the normal arrival allowance.
